n: Moab is urged to send lambs as tribute to Judah’s king in Zion, as Moab once paid Israel in lambs. Submitting to David’s throne is Moab’s path to safety.

f.g: “Rock” — a stronghold in Edom, possibly later Petra.

n: Moab’s women, like baby birds pushed from the nest, flutter helplessly at the river crossings of the Arnon.

f.g: Crossings of the Arnon River, Moab’s northern border.

n: Moab’s refugees plead with Judah: give us advice and fairness; shelter us like shade at noon; hide the fugitives and don’t betray them.

f.w: make thy shadow as the night

n: Let Moab’s outcasts stay with you; shelter them from the destroyer. When the oppressor is gone, peace will come.
Then a throne will be set up in mercy. A faithful ruler from David’s house will judge justly and quickly do what is right — a picture fully realized in the Messiah.

f.w: in mercy shall the throne be established

n: But Judah has heard of Moab’s great pride, arrogance, and anger. Its boasting is empty.

f.w: his lies shall not be so
f.g: His idle boasts amount to nothing.

n: So Moab will wail for itself, mourning the raisin cakes of Kir-hareseth, now gone.

f.g: Possibly “raisin cakes,” a delicacy of the region.

n: The fields of Heshbon and the famous vines of Sibmah, which once spread to Jazer and the desert and even toward the sea, have been trampled by foreign rulers.

f.g: A town famed for its vineyards.
Rulers of the nations — the invaders.

n: Isaiah weeps with the people of Jazer for the vines of Sibmah and drenches Heshbon and Elealeh with his tears. The joyful shouts of harvest have stopped.

f.w: I will water thee with my tears

n: Joy and gladness are gone from the orchards; no one sings in the vineyards or treads grapes in the winepress. God has silenced the harvest songs.

f.g: People who crushed grapes with their feet.

n: Isaiah’s heart throbs like a harp’s strings with grief for Moab. Even in judgment, God’s prophet feels compassion.

f.g: The inner self — seat of the emotions.

n: Moab will wear itself out at its pagan high places and go to its temple to pray, but its idols cannot help.
This is what the Lord has said about Moab in the past.

But now He says: within three years, counted exactly as a hired worker counts his contract, Moab’s glory will be despised and few will survive. Assyria campaigned through the region in the following years.

f.w: as the years of an hireling
f.g: Precisely counted — a hired laborer works not a day more than agreed.
